summary: Aspect B (tools and evidence): p02 plus the heart-rate rise ledger (hr_rise_ledger: ST persisting after heart rate is back at baseline, size, duration and load of the preceding heart-rate rise, and the ST change of the patient's comparable heart-rate rises) in the dossier, with a tool description that reads each measurement in both directions from verified cards (K01, K02, K04, K05 for; K10, K14, K36 against; K03, K07, K08, K42, K43 as cautions).

descriptions.annotator_reference: The candidate re-judged against an automatic time-varying ST reference built like that of Smrdel & Jager (2002), who approximated the Long-Term ST Database annotators' reference. The database annotators measured ST deviations from an ST reference function joined from local references placed in non-ischaemic stretches (K22); candidates here are detected against a record-wide median instead. Per involved lead: peak_deviation_uv signed towards the candidate (positive = same direction) against the record-wide median and after each step (after_slow_trend: 30-min mean, or 4-h mean where the two differ by more than 50 uV; after_steps: inside such stretches that contain an ST step or a QRS-shape step the reference follows the ST level; annotator_like_reference: deviations opposite to the lead's orientation, or under 25 uV in a lead of no orientation, absorbed); episode_at_100_uv and episode_at_150_uv (the LTSTDB episode rule re-applied against the final reference: start beyond 50 uV, at least 30 s at or beyond the threshold, overlapping the candidate); first_step_dropping_it_below_100_uv (none, slow_trend, step or orientation; judged on the peak only); the lead's orientation (E, D or U, from deviations outside this candidate) and the reference slope during the candidate. How to read it, in both directions: episode_at_150_uv true in an involved lead means the change still stands out as an episode against a reference that follows slow trends, steps and the lead's usual orientation, which counts for a genuine transient ST episode (it does not by itself separate ischemic from heart-rate related change). episode_at_100_uv false in every involved lead means such a reference absorbs the change, which counts against a new ischemic episode; first_step_dropping_it_below_100_uv names how (slow_trend: a drift or shifted level of the lead; step: together with an ST or QRS-shape step, as with a position, axis or conduction change; orientation: a deviation opposite to the lead's usual direction). True at 100 uV and false at 150 uV is the uncertain zone (Smrdel & Jager needed 150 uV with their automatic reference to match the database annotations), which counts in neither direction. A long real episode can pull the 30-min trend along and be partly absorbed: if the candidate is long and its onset and offset are gradual, check the ST trend before trusting an absorbed result. Evidence to weigh with the rest, not a verdict. A measurement packet, not a diagnosis.
descriptions.hr_rise_ledger: This candidate against the patient's own heart-rate rises, at the candidate's peak lead, with ST signed towards the candidate's extremum (positive = same direction); the same packet is in the dossier. this_candidate: hr_baseline_bpm (median heart rate 30 to 10 min before onset); hr_max_before_extremum_bpm and hr_rise_bpm (maximum from 10 min before onset to the ST extremum, and that maximum minus the baseline); hr_max_minus_st_extremum_s (negative: heart rate peaked before the ST extremum); minutes_at_baseline_plus_10_bpm (from 30 min before onset to the extremum); hr_load_60_min_before_bpm_min (heart rate above the record's 10th percentile, summed over the hour before onset); s_hr_back_to_baseline_while_st_at_half_or_more (from the extremum to 10 min after the candidate's end: seconds with heart rate within 5 bpm of the baseline while ST is still at half the extremum or more). comparable_rises_summary and largest_comparable_rises: the record's other heart-rate rises of 10 bpm or more within 10 min, outside this candidate +-10 min, that start within 10 bpm of this baseline and peak within 10 bpm of this candidate's maximum; st_change_uv is ST in the 75 s after that rise's heart-rate peak minus ST at its start, so a slower ST response there is under-counted; they can include the patient's other ST episodes (match their times with rate_response surges, which carry in_st_episode, or with episode_context's neighbouring candidates). How to read it, in both directions. For ischemia: ST still at half the extremum or more for a minute or more after heart rate is back near baseline (K01: in most ischemic episodes heart rate had returned to baseline while ST was still depressed; K02: ST depression continuing while heart rate falls); a large and long heart-rate rise before the extremum, or a high heart-rate load in the previous hour (K04: the likelihood of ischemia is proportional to the magnitude and duration of the heart-rate increase; K05: the duration of the increase influences the ischemic heart-rate threshold); several comparable rises of which few reached half this extremum (fraction_at_least_half low, this_extremum_minus_that_median_uv large), which means the heart-rate rise alone does not reproduce this change in this patient; one or two flat rises are weak evidence, because ischemia followed only 80% of threshold crossings (K03) and the threshold varies within a patient (K07). Against ischemia: s_hr_back_to_baseline_while_st_at_half_or_more at zero, with ST resolving as heart rate falls, in a change confined to sinus rates around 130 bpm or more (K10: such depression occurs in healthy volunteers during tachycardia); no heart-rate rise (hr_rise_bpm under 10 and almost no minutes at baseline + 10) together with an abrupt onset fits a position shift or artifact (K14, K36), although some ischemic episodes start with no heart-rate rise (K08); most comparable rises outside ST episodes reaching half this extremum or more means this patient's ST responds this way to such rises, which fits a heart-rate related change. When the comparable rises that reached it are the patient's other ST episodes, the similarity counts in neither direction: a patient's ischemic episodes recur at similar onset heart rates (K42), and separate episodes in one person may have different mechanisms (K43). No comparable rises: no comparison either way. Differences of one or two 15-s windows are within the time resolution. Evidence to weigh with the rest, not a verdict. A measurement packet, not a diagnosis.
